newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Lebanon wants Arab summit over peace -minister.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon wants Arab summit over peace -minister.

text.p: Lebanon's Foreign Minister Faris Bouez said on Tuesday the Israeli government did not want peace and Arabs needed to hold a summit to face the situation.

"We hope for an Arab summit, and whether it will be a large or a limited summit is not the most important issue. We have to set up a new view since peace is not assured under this Israeli government," Bouez told reporters at the end of a three-day visit to Tunisia.
"We call for such a meeting....and there are efforts now by other Arab countries such as Syria and Egypt towards that aim," he added.
Bouez said he discussed the matter with Tunisian President Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali on Tuesday.

"For us, it is clear that (Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu does not want peace...and the United States has frozen its efforts in the peace process at the demand of the Israeli government," he said.

Israel's negotiations with the Palestinians came to a halt after Israel broke ground for a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem last month. Peace talks with Lebanon and Syria have been frozen for more than a year.
